title: Endpoint Engineer (Senior)
description:
Computer World Services, Corp. (CWS) seeks a Senior Endpoint Engineer to design, maintain, secure, automate, and modernize enterprise endpoint capabilities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program, including endpoint images, application packaging, device provisioning, software deployment, patching, configuration baselines, and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI).

The engineer supports physical and virtual endpoints throughout their lifecycle across USMEPCOM Headquarters, MEPS, Remote Processing Substations, COOP locations, and remote users. The role maintains a clear division of responsibility with cybersecurity personnel who identify, prioritize, and validate findings, while the Endpoint Engineer tests and implements approved changes through change control and provides deployment evidence for validation.

Key Tasks & Responsibilities

• Serve as senior engineer for enterprise endpoint imaging, packaging, deployment, patching, configuration, and VDI capabilities.

• Design, build, test, and maintain standardized endpoint images, including drivers, OS settings, security baselines, and required software, and establish image versioning, release, rollback, and retirement procedures.

• Develop automated deployment task sequences, provisioning workflows, enrollment processes, and configuration profiles using Microsoft Intune, Configuration Manager, Windows Autopilot, or comparable platforms.

• Package commercial, Government, and internally developed software with installation, detection, dependency, upgrade, and removal logic, and test and troubleshoot package deployments.

• Develop and maintain approved scripts and automation for provisioning, packaging, configuration, and remediation in version-control repositories.

• Design and administer endpoint patching for operating systems, applications, drivers, and firmware, establishing pilot groups, deployment rings, maintenance windows, and exception processes; test updates and monitor compliance.

• Engineer and support VDI base images, desktop pools, application delivery, and user profiles; troubleshoot login, profile, performance, and connectivity issues; and coordinate dependencies with virtualization, storage, network, and identity teams.

• Support endpoint deployment and refresh projects, OS upgrades, application migrations, and endpoint-management transitions, developing technical implementation plans.

• Provide Tier 3/Tier 4 engineering support for complex endpoint, packaging, deployment, patching, and VDI incidents, including major incidents and root-cause corrective actions, and improve Service Desk and field-support knowledge content.

• Review cybersecurity findings assigned to endpoint operations, assess operational impact and rollback needs, implement approved remediation through change and release procedures, and provide completion evidence; apply DISA STIGs and endpoint-security baselines.

• Maintain endpoint inventories, image and package records, patch status, VDI documentation, SOPs, and deployment and rollback plans, and provide endpoint health and compliance information for program reporting.

Education & Experience

Required:

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience where permitted by the labor category.

• Minimum of eight (8) years of relevant experience in endpoint engineering, systems engineering, device management, desktop engineering, VDI engineering, or a related discipline.

• Experience designing and maintaining enterprise endpoint images and developing, testing, and deploying application packages.

• Experience supporting endpoint provisioning, deployment, patching, configuration, lifecycle management, and VDI.

• Experience implementing endpoint-security or vulnerability-remediation changes using controlled testing, phased deployment, validation, and rollback practices.

• Strong written, verbal, analytical, and technical problem-solving skills.

title: Head of Logistics & Planning
description:
ABOUT US

We're building the next generation of the TV operating system, reimagining the experience at the intersection of television, streaming, and how people discover and search.

THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Head of Logistics & Planning. You'll plan how much of our first hardware product we hold, where it sits, and how it reaches every customer. You'll own demand and inventory planning across our website, retailers and marketplaces, plus the logistics behind it: inbound shipments, US customs, the work with our 3PL partner, delivery to customers, retail compliance and returns. Then you'll take us into new countries, starting with Canada.

 

You won't start with a team. Instead, you'll build a set of AI agents and supervise them, alongside our 3PL, freight forwarder and customs broker. Your agents handle the daily matching, tracking and chasing, so your time goes on the plan, our partners and the exceptions. You decide what each agent does, set its limits and check its work. Anything above those limits comes to you, and you own every promise we make to a retailer. As we grow, you decide when the next person joins and what they own.

You'll report to our President and work on-site in Redwood City, with regular time at our 3PL's warehouse and occasional travel to new markets.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the demand and inventory plan. Forecast demand by channel, set stock levels and reorder points, and propose how much goes to our website and each retailer. Give hardware operations the forecast that sets our factory orders.

- Run our 3PL partnership. Finish onboarding our 3PL partner and connect it to our store and each retailer. Set service levels and a weekly scorecard, reconcile inventory and audit invoices. Track landed cost and the cost to serve each order and channel, and negotiate with our 3PL, carriers and freight partners.

- Bring product into the US. Own freight from our factory in Asia to the warehouse. Book and manage our freight forwarder, plan arrivals with hardware operations, and own US customs with our broker (tariff classification, duty, the customs bond and filings).

- Deliver to customers. Own direct-to-consumer fulfillment: carriers, shipping rates, delivery promises, exceptions and order-status updates, working with customer support.

- Make us an easy vendor for retailers. Set up logistics with each retailer and marketplace: electronic orders and shipping notices (EDI), barcodes and carton labels, routing guides and on-time-in-full targets. Dispute chargebacks we don't owe.

- Run returns. Set the rules for grading, restocking and refurbishing returned units, and report why products come back.

- Build and supervise your agent team. Design the agents that forecast, track, reconcile, check compliance and draft disputes. Connect them to our 3PL, EDI, carriers and store, set what each one may approve, and audit their work every week.

- Open new countries, starting with Canada. Choose how we import and fulfill in each market. With our advisers, set up the customs, tax and recycling registrations, then launch on schedule.

WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH IN YOUR FIRST SIX MONTHS

- Launch on time. Our 3PL is connected to our store before the first shipment arrives, and launch orders go out on schedule.

- One plan the company runs on. A weekly demand and inventory plan by channel that leadership reviews, and that drives factory orders and allocation.

- Ready for retail. EDI is tested with each retailer before its first purchase order, and first shipments meet each routing guide.

- Agents doing real work. At least three agents run every day, for example on inventory reconciliation, shipment tracking and chargeback disputes. Each has a limit on what it can approve, a log of what it did and a monthly accuracy check.

- A Canada plan ready to approve. How we import, where we hold stock, which registrations we need, and a launch date.

WHAT YOU BRING

- 8+ years across demand planning, inventory analysis, supply chain

Wade Trim has been developing solutions to complex engineering and planning challenges for a century to deliver water and sewer services to residents and businesses, keep traffic flowing smoothly and safely, treat wastewater and stormwater to protect our waterways, distribute reliable power to customers, and provide community spaces to enjoy.
